deck_name: 君の名は。 Ch.2 端緒 — Grammar & Expressions
source: 新海誠『君の名は。』(角川つばさ文庫), 第二章「端緒」
notes: Grammar, casual speech and Itomori dialect for Chapter 2. Chapter 2 starts on p.9. Cards from pp.9 and 12–21 are checked against the printed pages and come first, in page order (pp.10–11 weren't photographed; their cards are marked). Cards after that are built from the chapter's scenes and the novel's style and say 'Not yet checked' in their scene — some of them may turn out to belong to Chapter 3. Example sentences are original, not quoted from the book.

priority_guide.high: Learn before or while reading this chapter — it carries the scene.
priority_guide.medium: Useful; context usually helps if you forget it.
priority_guide.low: Recognition is enough — look it up once, don't over-drill.

difficulty_guide.two_above: N1 / literary — ambitious; learn to recognise it.

kanji_difficulty_guide.easy: Kanji are common; readable at N3.
kanji_difficulty_guide.medium: One or more kanji may trip you — drill the reading.
kanji_difficulty_guide.hard: Rare kanji or irregular reading — learn the kana form first.

cards.pattern: い-adj stem / な-adj + げ (げな + N, げに + V); Vたい → 〜たげ
cards.scene: p.9 — The girl's voice in 瀧's dream sounds lonely and anxious (寂しげ・不安げ), the first of many 〜げ words in this chapter.
cards.context: Form: 寂しい → 寂しげ, 楽しい → 楽しげ, 不安 → 不安げ; Vたい → 〜たげ (もの問いたげ = looking as if wanting to ask). It behaves as a な-adjective: 寂しげな声, 誇らしげに. Like 〜そう (looks ~) but more literary: it describes the air a person or thing gives off. Spot it again on p.13 (楽しげ), p.15 (怪しげ), p.17 (後ろめたげ) and p.20 (誇らしげ). Irregular: いい → よさげ.
cards.example_sentence: 彼は何か言いたげな顔でこちらを見ていた。
cards.example_reading: かれ は なにか いいたげな かお で こちら を みて いた。
cards.example_meaning: He was looking at me as if he wanted to say something.

cards.word: すげえ・やべえ (〜い → 〜えー)
meanings: rough male sound change in い-adjectives
cards.scene: p.12 — 瀧: 女の体ってすげえな / すげえリアル.
cards.context: Form: the last two vowel sounds of an い-adjective merge into a long え: すごい → すげえ, やばい → やべえ, うるさい → うるせえ, 痛い → いてえ, ない → ねえ (知らねえ). Rough, masculine, very casual. Also written with ー: すげー.
cards.example_sentence: うわ、この景色すげえ！
cards.example_reading: うわ、 この けしき すげえ！
cards.example_meaning: Whoa, this view is amazing!
cards.pattern: 〜ない → 〜ねえ, 〜ごい → 〜げえ, 〜ばい → 〜べえ, 〜さい → 〜せえ

cards.scene: p.12 四葉: なにしとるの？; p.19 ちゃんとしとるな, 溜まっとるんよ; p.21 the polite しとります.
cards.context: Form: 〜ている → 〜とる (from 〜ておる). 何しとるの? (= 何しているの?), 知っとる (= 知っている), 見とった (= 見ていた). After a voiced て it becomes 〜どる: 読んどる (= 読んでいる).
cards.example_sentence: お母さん、台所で何しとるの？
cards.example_reading: おかあさん、 だいどころ で なに しとる の？
cards.example_meaning: Mum, what are you doing in the kitchen?
cards.pattern: Vて → 〜とる / 〜どる (= 〜ている)
N / Vます-stem + がち (→ 〜がちな N)
cards.scene: p.12 — 瀧 takes in the little girl: about ten, twin tails, rather upturned eyes (ツリ目がち), a cheeky look.
cards.context: Form: noun or Vます-stem + がち, used as a な-adjective (〜がちな N). Main use: tends to (something undesirable): 忘れがち, 遅れがち, 病気がち. With looks it means 'rather, on the ~ side': ツリ目がち (rather upturned eyes), 伏し目がち (eyes often lowered). Compare 〜気味 (ぎみ, slightly ~) and 〜っぽい (~ish).
cards.example_sentence: 冬は運動不足になりがちだ。
cards.example_reading: ふゆ は うんどう ぶそく に なりがち だ。
cards.example_meaning: In winter you tend not to get enough exercise.

cards.pattern: (situation) + ていうことは / ってことは、〜？
cards.scene: p.12 — The girl calls him お姉ちゃん, so 瀧 reasons: which means… this kid is my sister?
cards.context: Form: ていうことは / ってことは at the start of a sentence, drawing a conclusion from what was just said or seen. A casual clipped form of ということは (と drops or becomes っ). Same family: ていうか / っていうか (or rather). Often ends in a question or 〜ってこと？
cards.example_sentence: 明日は休み？ていうことは、今夜は遅くまで起きていられるね。
cards.example_reading: あした は やすみ？ ていう こと は、 こんや は おそく まで おきて いられる ね。
cards.example_meaning: Tomorrow's a day off? Which means we can stay up late tonight.

cards.pattern: Vます-stem + きる
cards.scene: p.12 — The little girl gives him an utterly exasperated look (呆れきった) and orders him to breakfast.
cards.context: Form: Vます-stem + きる (a 五段 verb; written 切る or kana). Two senses: do all of it (食べきる eat it all, 使いきる use up, 読みきる read to the end) and 'to the extreme' with states (疲れきる exhausted, 冷えきる chilled through, 呆れきる utterly fed up). Negative 〜きれない = can't finish / can't fully: 数えきれない (countless).
cards.example_sentence: マラソンを走りきったあと、彼は疲れきって座り込んだ。
cards.example_reading: マラソン を はしりきった あと、 かれ は つかれきって すわりこんだ。
cards.example_meaning: After running the whole marathon, he sat down, completely exhausted.

cards.pattern: Vます-stem + ない (= 〜なさい): 来ない (きない), しない, 行きない
cards.scene: p.12 — 四葉 snaps at her half-asleep 'sister': breakfast, come on, quick! (早く来ない！). It's an order, not 'won't come'.
cards.context: Form: Vます-stem + ない, shortened from 〜なさい: 来なさい → 来ない (furigana き: きない, not こない), 行きなさい → 行きない, しなさい → しない. For する and る-verbs it looks exactly like the negative, which is the trap: p.17 仲直りしないよ？ means 'make up already, OK?', not 'you won't make up?'. The ！ or よ and the situation tell you it's an order.
cards.example_sentence: 雨降っとるで、傘持っていきない！
cards.example_reading: あめ ふっとる で、 かさ もって いきない！
cards.example_meaning: It's raining, so take an umbrella!

cards.pattern: V-る + の → 〜んの (寝ぼけとるの → 寝ぼけとんの)
cards.scene: p.12 — 四葉 asks her oddly behaving 'sister' whether she's still half asleep (寝ぼけとんの？).
cards.context: Form: る before の turns into ん: 寝ぼけとるの → 寝ぼけとんの (= 寝ぼけているの), 何しとんの (= 何しているの). Casual standard speech does the same (何してんの, 分かんない). On p.19 サヤちん's オカルトにしんの！ is usually taken as local するの ('you turn everything into the occult!'); some readers hear the negative しん (= しない) + scolding の ('stop…!'). Either way it's exasperated scolding.
cards.example_sentence: こんな時間まで何しとんの？もう二時やよ。
cards.example_reading: こんな じかん まで なに しとん の？ もう にじ や よ。
cards.example_meaning: What are you doing up at this hour? It's already two o'clock!

cards.pattern: 普通形 + かのように (N / なA: である + かのように)
cards.scene: p.13 — as if the body were insisting it had grown up healthy (主張しているかのような).
cards.context: Form: plain form (N / な-adjective usually + である) + かのように. Compares with something that is not actually true: まるで何もなかったかのように. More literary than 〜みたいに or 〜ように; the か adds 'as if (though it isn't)'.
cards.example_sentence: 彼はまるで何も知らないかのように、平気な顔をしていた。
cards.example_reading: かれ は まるで なにも しらない か の よう に、 へいき な かお を して いた。
cards.example_meaning: He kept a calm face, as if he knew nothing at all.

cards.pattern: 普通形 / Nの / なAな + くせに
cards.scene: p.14 — a kid who hasn't even lost her baby teeth, yet acts like the grown-up (子どものくせに).
cards.context: Form: plain form / Nの / なAな + くせに. Like 〜のに, but with contempt or reproach toward a person: 男のくせに, 知らないくせに (you don't even know, and yet...). Used about other people (or yourself, mockingly), never neutrally.
cards.example_sentence: 自分は遅刻するくせに、人には厳しいんだから。
cards.example_reading: じぶん は ちこく する くせ に、 ひと に は きびしい ん だ から。
cards.example_meaning: He's always late himself, yet he's strict with everyone else.

cards.pattern: N + の代わりに / V(plain) + 代わりに
cards.scene: p.14 — Instead of saying sorry to 四葉 for being late, 三葉 just announces she'll make breakfast tomorrow.
cards.context: Form: N + の代わりに; V (dictionary / た) + 代わりに. Here the noun is a quoted word: ごめんの代わりに = instead of (saying) 'sorry'. It can also mean 'in exchange for': 手伝う代わりに (in return for helping). 代わり alone: お代わり (a second helping).
cards.example_sentence: お礼の代わりに、彼女は手作りのクッキーをくれた。
cards.example_reading: おれい の かわり に、 かのじょ は てづくり の クッキー を くれた。
cards.example_meaning: Instead of a thank-you, she gave me homemade cookies.

cards.pattern: plain-form clause + 節がある
cards.scene: p.14 — 三葉 notes that 四葉, who still has baby teeth, seems to have decided she's more grown-up than her big sister.
cards.context: Form: plain-form clause + 節がある (also 節が見られる, 節もある). 節 (ふし) here = a point or telltale sign: an inference from how someone behaves, often a little critical: 自分が正しいと思っている節がある. Adult, written register; softer than 〜に違いない. 節 on its own (ふし) also means a joint, a knot, or a melody line.
cards.example_sentence: 弟は、自分が一番頭がいいと思っている節がある。
cards.example_reading: おとうと は、 じぶん が いちばん あたま が いい と おもって いる ふし が ある。
cards.example_meaning: My little brother seems to think he's the smartest of us all.

cards.pattern: Vます-stem + つつ / つつも; N / な-adj + でありつつ(も)
cards.scene: p.14 — 三葉 serves herself rice while thinking she mustn't show weakness by apologising (思いつつ); on p.16 grandma, past eighty and always in kimono, voices her anger without a word (でありつつも).
cards.context: Form: Vます-stem + つつ (= ながら, written register): 思いつつ (while thinking). つつも adds 'although, despite': 悪いと知りつつも (though I knew it was wrong). With nouns and な-adjectives use であり + つつ(も): 着物姿でありつつも. Related: 〜つつある = to be in the process of (増えつつある).
cards.example_sentence: 体に悪いと分かりつつも、夜中にラーメンを食べてしまった。
cards.example_reading: からだ に わるい と わかりつつ も、 よなか に ラーメン を たべて しまった。
cards.example_meaning: Even though I knew it was bad for me, I ended up eating noodles in the middle of the night.

cards.pattern: N (usually a kanji compound) + 的 → な-adj (〜的な N / 〜的に)
cards.scene: p.14 — 四葉's aggressive tone (攻撃的) greets 三葉; later the speaker blares at violent volume (暴力的, p.15), the town is very Japanese and very 昭和 (p.18), and her father's speech is high-handed (高圧的, p.21).
cards.context: Form: N + 的 → な-adjective: 攻撃的な声 (an aggressive voice), 暴力的な音量 (violently loud volume), 個人的に (personally). It turns a noun into 'having the quality of'. 新海誠 stacks them for humour: 日本的昭和的 = 'so Japanese, so 昭和-era'. Slang stretches it further: わたし的には = 'as for me'.
cards.example_sentence: 彼の話は具体的で、とても分かりやすかった。
cards.example_reading: かれ の はなし は ぐたいてき で、 とても わかりやすかった。
cards.example_meaning: His explanation was concrete and very easy to follow.

cards.pattern: plain form + で(ね) (= から(ね))
cards.scene: p.14 — Instead of apologising for being late, 三葉 declares that tomorrow she'll do the cooking (作るでね！).
cards.context: Form: plain form + で, often + ね / な: 作るでね (= 作るからね), 行くで (= 行くから). Central Japan speech (岐阜, 愛知, 飛騨); this で marks a reason or an announcement, not the particle で 'at / by'. Used to declare a decision or justify yourself: 'I'll do it, so there!'.
cards.example_sentence: 東京のお土産、ちゃんと買ってくるでね！
cards.example_reading: とうきょう の おみやげ、 ちゃんと かって くる で ね！
cards.example_meaning: I'll bring you back a souvenir from Tokyo, I promise!

cards.scene: p.15 grandma: 今日は普通やなあ; p.18 失礼やな; p.19 そうや.
cards.context: Form: Noun / な-adjective + や. 嫌や (= 嫌だ), そうや (= そうだ), 何や (= 何だ), 〜やった (= だった), 〜やない (= じゃない). Typical of western Japan (Kansai, Gifu/Hida). Itomori's speech is modelled on 飛騨弁.
cards.example_sentence: もう、こんな雨の日は嫌や。
cards.example_reading: もう、 こんな あめ の ひ は いや や。
cards.example_meaning: Ugh, I hate rainy days like this.
cards.pattern: Noun / な-adj + や (= だ)
plain form + もん / もんなあ / もんね
cards.scene: p.15 — Grandma remarks that 三葉 is normal today, and 四葉 grins: well, yesterday was crazy (ヤバかったもんなあ).
cards.context: Form: plain form + もん (casual もの), often + なあ / ね / な. It gives a reason or justification with feeling: だって知らなかったもん (but I didn't know!). With なあ it's 'well, after all ~'. Sounds childish when pouting (行きたくないもん), neutral with なあ / ね. ヤバい = crazy, awful (slang; can also mean amazing).
cards.example_sentence: テッシーが怒るのも分かるよ。あれはひどかったもんなあ。
cards.example_reading: テッシー が おこる の も わかる よ。 あれ は ひどかった もん なあ。
cards.example_meaning: I get why テッシー's angry. That was pretty awful, after all.

cards.pattern: Vた + りして (sentence-final)
cards.scene: p.15 — 四葉 teases her: yesterday she went and screamed out of nowhere and all (悲鳴あげたりして).
cards.context: Form: Vた + りして at the end of a sentence, from 〜たり〜たりする with the rest dropped. It picks one example and leaves the rest hanging: 'going and screaming and stuff'. Also a teasing guess: 本当は好きだったりして？ (what if you actually like him?). Light and conversational.
cards.example_sentence: サヤちんって、実はテッシーのこと好きだったりして。
cards.example_reading: サヤちん って、 じつ は テッシー の こと すき だったり して。
cards.example_meaning: What if サヤちん actually likes テッシー?

cards.pattern: V / い-adj plain + に違いない; N / な-adj + に違いない (no だ)
cards.scene: p.15 — Under grandma's suspicious stare, 三葉 decides 四葉's smirk must be mocking her, and the narration adds （に違いない） in brackets.
cards.context: Form: V / い-adj plain form + に違いない; N / な-adj + に違いない (drop だ). A strong conviction from the speaker's own reasoning: stronger than だろう, more personal than はず (logical expectation). The book's joke: ばかにしている（に違いない） states it as fact, then the brackets admit it's only her assumption.
cards.example_sentence: 部屋の電気がついている。お母さんはもう帰っているに違いない。
cards.example_reading: へや の でんき が ついて いる。 おかあさん は もう かえって いる に ちがいない。
cards.example_meaning: The light's on in the room. Mum must be home already.

cards.pattern: N + だけに; な-adj + な + だけに; V / い-adj plain + だけに
cards.scene: p.16 — 糸守 is a shabby little town of 1,500, so, as you'd expect, almost everyone knows everyone.
cards.context: Form: N + だけに; な-adj + な + だけに; V / い-adj plain + だけに. 'Because X (a notable feature), naturally / all the more Y': 小さな町だけに = being the small town it is. More evaluative than から. Often with disappointment: 期待していただけに残念だ (all the more disappointing because I'd hoped). Not だけ 'only'.
cards.example_sentence: 人気の店だけに、平日でも一時間待ちだった。
cards.example_reading: にんき の みせ だけ に、 へいじつ でも いちじかん まち だった。
cards.example_meaning: Being such a popular place, there was an hour's wait even on a weekday.

cards.pattern: V / い-adj plain + (が)故に; N + (の / である)故に
cards.scene: p.16 — The speaker unit itself is out of reach, so grandma pulls the plug instead, told in mock-solemn 故に.
cards.context: Form: V / い-adj plain + (が)故に; N + (の / である)故に; sentence-initial 故に = therefore (as in maths proofs). Classical-flavoured 'because': 手が届かない故に = since it can't be reached. The narration uses grand language for unplugging a speaker, for comic effect. Also as a noun: 若さ故の過ち (a mistake born of youth).
cards.example_sentence: 彼は正直すぎるが故に、損をすることが多い。
cards.example_reading: かれ は しょうじき すぎる が ゆえ に、 そん を する こと が おおい。
cards.example_meaning: Because he's too honest, he often loses out.

cards.pattern: N + のごとく (= のように); N + のごとき + N; V + (が)ごとく
cards.scene: p.16 — Like a well-drilled team move (連係プレイ), 三葉 grabs the remote and switches on the TV the moment grandma unplugs the speaker.
cards.context: Form: N + の + ごとく (adverb, = のように); N + の + ごとき + N (= のような); V + (が)ごとく. Kanji 如く. Classical and written: today mostly in set phrases (いつものごとく = as always, 例のごとく = as usual) or for comic grandeur, as here.
cards.example_sentence: 兄はいつものごとく、昼過ぎまで寝ていた。
cards.example_reading: あに は いつも の ごとく、 ひるすぎ まで ねて いた。
cards.example_meaning: As usual, my brother slept until past noon.

cards.reading: にいちど / にいっぽん
cards.scene: p.17 — the comet that comes once every 1,200 years (千二百年に一度).
cards.context: Form: [time span] + に + [count]. 千年に一度 (once every thousand years), 一時間に一本 (one bus/train an hour), 週に三回 (three times a week). The counter changes with the thing counted: 本 for trains and buses, 度/回 for events.
cards.example_sentence: このバスは、一時間に一本しか来ない。
cards.example_reading: この バス は、 いちじかん に いっぽん しか こない。
cards.example_meaning: This bus only comes once an hour.
cards.pattern: Time span + に + 一度 / 一回 / 一本 …
N (time span / range) + にわたって / にわたり; にわたる + N
cards.scene: p.17 — The newsreader says the comet will be visible to the naked eye over several days (数日間にわたって).
cards.context: Form: N (time span, distance, range) + にわたって; formal にわたり; before a noun にわたる / にわたった: 三時間にわたる会議. Stresses the whole extent: 全国にわたって (nationwide), 十年にわたって (for a full ten years). News and written register; in speech, 〜の間ずっと.
cards.example_sentence: その工事は三か月にわたって続いた。
cards.example_reading: その こうじ は さんかげつ に わたって つづいた。
cards.example_meaning: The construction went on for three whole months.

cards.reading: とみられる / ており
cards.pattern: plain form + と見られる; Vて + おり (= 〜ていて)
cards.scene: p.17 — The TV report: the comet is expected to be observable with the naked eye (観測できると見られており), and research bodies worldwide are busy preparing.
cards.context: Form: plain form + と見られる (passive of 見る, 'is seen as / estimated to'), the cautious news phrasing for forecasts and unconfirmed facts; also と見られている, 〜と見られる男 (a man believed to be…). 〜ており is the formal connective of 〜ている (おる = formal いる): 準備を進めており、… Hear both together and you're in news Japanese.
cards.example_sentence: 台風は明日の朝に上陸すると見られており、注意が必要です。
cards.example_reading: たいふう は あした の あさ に じょうりく する と みられて おり、 ちゅうい が ひつよう です。
cards.example_meaning: The typhoon is expected to make landfall tomorrow morning, so caution is needed.

cards.pattern: N + をはじめ(として); N + をはじめとする / をはじめとした + N
cards.scene: p.17 — The news says research institutions around the world, JAXA among them, are busy preparing to observe the comet.
cards.context: Form: N + をはじめ(として), …; before a noun をはじめとする / をはじめとした + N (as in JAXAをはじめとした研究機関). Names the leading or most typical member of a group, then implies the rest. Usually written in kana (始め). Formal; in speech you'd say 〜とか〜など.
cards.example_sentence: この町には、温泉をはじめとして、たくさんの観光地がある。
cards.example_reading: この まち に は、 おんせん を はじめ と して、 たくさん の かんこうち が ある。
cards.example_meaning: This town has lots of sights, starting with its hot springs.

cards.pattern: なにが + N / quoted phrase + よ
cards.scene: p.17 — After snapping 'grown-up problem!' at 四葉, 三葉 fumes to herself: what's so special about a mayoral election anyway?
cards.context: Form: なにが + (a word someone used, or the topic) + よ (feminine casual; men say なにが〜だ). A rhetorical rejection: you pick up a word and throw it back with contempt: なにが「大丈夫」よ (what do you mean, 'it's fine'?!). Sarcastic and irritated.
cards.example_sentence: なにが「すぐ終わる」よ。もう二時間も待ってるじゃない。
cards.example_reading: なに が 「すぐ おわる」 よ。 もう にじかん も まってる じゃない。
cards.example_meaning: 'It'll be over quickly', my foot! I've been waiting two hours already.

meanings: (it) is, you know (= だよ / なんだ)
cards.scene: p.18 — テッシー: 重いんやさ (she's heavy, you know).
cards.context: Form: Noun / plain form + (なん)やさ. Roughly だよ or なんだ — explaining or asserting gently: そうやさ (that's right, you know), 決まりなんやさ (it's the rule, you see). Very characteristic of the Hida region.
cards.example_sentence: この祭りは、昔からの決まりなんやさ。
cards.example_reading: この まつり は、 むかし から の きまり なん やさ。
cards.example_meaning: This festival is a custom from long ago, you see.
cards.pattern: Noun / plain form + (なん)やさ (= だよ / なんだ)
N / Vます-stem + っぷり (emphatic form of ぶり)
cards.scene: p.18 — When 三葉 says they get along, テッシー and サヤちん both shout that they do NOT, and the earnestness of their denial makes her giggle.
cards.context: Form: N / Vます-stem + ぶり, with っ for emphasis → っぷり: 否定っぷり (the way they deny it), 食べっぷり (the way someone eats), 飲みっぷり, 仕事ぶり. Describes a striking, almost admirable manner. A different 〜ぶり from Ch.1: time span + ぶり = 'for the first time in ~' (三年ぶり).
cards.example_sentence: サヤちんの見事な食べっぷりに、みんな驚いた。
cards.example_reading: サヤちん の みごとな たべっぷり に、 みんな おどろいた。
cards.example_meaning: Everyone was amazed at how heartily サヤちん ate.

cards.pattern: ど + N (colloquial emphasis)
cards.scene: p.18 — Taking in the shining lake and green mountains, 三葉 sums it up: they live in the very back of beyond (ど田舎).
cards.context: Form: ど + noun, from western-Japan speech and now nationwide slang: ど田舎 (the middle of nowhere), ど真ん中 (dead centre), ど素人 (a complete amateur), ど根性 (sheer guts), どストライク (right in my strike zone). Rough and emphatic; keep it out of polite speech.
cards.example_sentence: 祖父の家は、バスが一日二本しか来ないど田舎にある。
cards.example_reading: そふ の いえ は、 バス が いちにち にほん しか こない どいなか に ある。
cards.example_meaning: My grandfather's house is out in the total sticks, where the bus comes just twice a day.

cards.pattern: time span + 来 (+ の N)
cards.scene: p.18 — 三葉, テッシー and サヤちん have been best friends for ten years now (十年来の親友).
cards.context: Form: time span + 来 (らい), often + の + N: 十年来の親友 (friends of ten years' standing), 二十年来の夢, or adverbially 昨年来 (since last year). The same 来 as 以来 (いらい, since). Formal and written-sounding; in speech you'd say 十年前から.
cards.example_sentence: これは祖父の三十年来の夢だった。
cards.example_reading: これ は そふ の さんじゅうねん らい の ゆめ だった。
cards.example_meaning: This had been my grandfather's dream for thirty years.

cards.scene: p.19 — 'she says it's done properly today' (〜ちゃんとしてるって).
cards.context: Form: plain form / N + って = と / という / と言っていた. 来ないって = (they said) they're not coming. As a topic: 彗星って何? = what's a comet, anyway? Very common in dialogue.
cards.example_sentence: サヤちん、明日は来られないって。
cards.example_reading: サヤちん、 あした は こられない って。
cards.example_meaning: Saya-chin says she can't come tomorrow.
cards.pattern: Plain form / N + って
plain form + のではないか
cards.scene: p.19 — 三葉 secretly suspects they suit each other (お似合いなのではないか).
cards.context: Form: plain form + のではないか (Na-adj / N + なのではないか); spoken 〜んじゃないか. In narration it is not a question to anyone — it voices a growing suspicion: もしかして、あの人なのではないか. On the certainty scale it sits above 〜かもしれない and below 〜に違いない.
cards.example_sentence: もしかしたら、あの人も誰かを探しているのではないか。
cards.example_reading: もしかしたら、 あの ひと も だれか を さがして いる の では ない か。
cards.example_meaning: Could it be that that person, too, is searching for someone?

cards.pattern: い-adj stem + め (→ noun / な-adj; 〜めに)
cards.scene: p.19 — テッシー is lanky, with a shaven head that's a bit on the uncool side (ダサめ).
cards.context: Form: い-adjective stem + め: 大きめ (largish), 早めに (a bit early), 少なめ (on the light side); ダサい (uncool) → ダサめ. Kanji 目, usually written in kana. Handy when ordering: ご飯少なめで (less rice, please). Not the insulting suffix N + め (あいつめ! = that wretch!).
cards.example_sentence: 明日は雨らしいから、早めに家を出よう。
cards.example_reading: あした は あめ らしい から、 はやめ に いえ を でよう。
cards.example_meaning: It's supposed to rain tomorrow, so let's leave the house a bit early.

cards.pattern: V(plain) + ふう (だ / に / な); N + 風
cards.scene: p.19 — テッシー and サヤちん always look as if they're squabbling, yet their back-and-forth is perfectly timed; 三葉 secretly thinks they suit each other.
cards.context: Form: V plain + ふう (風) = appearance only: いがみ合っているふう = seeming to be at each other's throats (but not really). N + 風 = in the style of: 和風 (Japanese-style), 学生風の男 (a student-looking man). Close to 〜ように見える / 〜みたい; 〜ふりをする is deliberate pretending.
cards.example_sentence: 彼は興味がないふうを装っていたが、本当は話を全部聞いていた。
cards.example_reading: かれ は きょうみ が ない ふう を よそおって いた が、 ほんとう は はなし を ぜんぶ きいて いた。
cards.example_meaning: He acted as if he wasn't interested, but he was actually listening to every word.

meanings: is ~, I tell you! (= だぜ)
cards.pattern: N / な-adj + やぜ (= だぜ)
cards.scene: p.19 — テッシー is convinced yesterday's strangeness was definitely fox possession (狐憑きやぜ！).
cards.context: Form: N / な-adj + や (local copula, = だ) + ぜ (rough, boyish 'I'm telling you'). やぜ = だぜ. テッシー mixes 糸守 や with masculine ぜ; also heard: やな (= だな), やろ (= だろう). 狐憑き (きつねつき) = possession by a fox spirit, a folk explanation for sudden strange behaviour.
cards.example_sentence: あの店のラーメン、絶対に町で一番やぜ！
cards.example_reading: あの みせ の ラーメン、 ぜったい に まち で いちばん や ぜ！
cards.example_meaning: That shop's noodles are the best in town, no question!

meanings: probably / right? (= だろう / でしょう)
cards.scene: p.21 — the crowd: 今期も宮水さんで決まりやろ.
cards.context: Form: plain form + やろ. そうやろ? (right?), 来るやろ (they'll probably come). Rising tone = 'isn't it?'; falling tone = a guess. 〜やろか = だろうか (I wonder).
cards.example_sentence: 明日は晴れるやろ。
cards.example_reading: あした は はれる やろ。
cards.example_meaning: It'll probably be sunny tomorrow.
cards.pattern: Plain form + やろ (= だろう)
Vて + はじめて
cards.scene: p.21 — 'only once that is achieved…' (実現して初めて).
cards.context: Form: Vて + はじめて (初めて). 'Only once X happened did Y' — usually followed by a realization: 失ってはじめて大切さに気づく (you only see its value after losing it). Different from plain 初めて (for the first time).
cards.example_sentence: 社会人になってはじめて、親のありがたさがわかった。
cards.example_reading: しゃかいじん に なって はじめて、 おや の ありがたさ が わかった。
cards.example_meaning: Only after I became a working adult did I understand how much I owed my parents.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): The opening compares the dream to being a nursing baby (〜のように); まるで often leads such comparisons in 新海誠's narration.
cards.context: Form: まるで + N の / plain form + ように (adverb) / ような (before a noun); casual: みたいに / みたいな. まるで flags a striking comparison: まるで夢のようだ.
cards.example_sentence: 雪の朝、町はまるで絵のように静かだった。
cards.example_reading: ゆき の あさ、 まち は まるで え の よう に しずか だった。
cards.example_meaning: On the snowy morning, the town was as still as a painting.
cards.pattern: まるで + N の / plain form + ように・ような

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): News and gossip about the comet: what everyone has heard.
cards.context: Form: plain form + らしい (N / な-adj drop だ). Information you got from someone else or the news. Different from 〜らしい meaning 'typical of' (男らしい) and from 〜そうだ (a more direct report of what was said).
cards.example_sentence: 今夜は、彗星がよく見えるらしい。
cards.example_reading: こんや は、 すいせい が よく みえる らしい。
cards.example_meaning: Apparently the comet will be easy to see tonight.
cards.pattern: Plain form + らしい

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): Itomori speech makes verbs negative with 〜ん: 知らん, 分からん.
cards.context: Form: Vない-stem + ん. 知らん (= 知らない), 分からん (= 分からない), 行かん (= 行かない), せん (= しない), こん (= 来ない). Not the explanatory ん of 〜んだ — check what comes before it.
cards.example_sentence: そんな話、ぜんぜん知らん。
cards.example_reading: そんな はなし、 ぜんぜん しらん。
cards.example_meaning: I've never heard anything like that.
cards.pattern: Vない-stem + ん (= 〜ない)

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): Itomori speakers say ええ for いい.
cards.context: Form: いい → ええ. ええよ (= いいよ, sure / OK), ええなあ (= いいなあ, lucky you), もうええ (= もういい, never mind / that's enough). Don't confuse it with the polite 'yes' ええ — tone and context tell them apart.
cards.example_sentence: 東京はええなあ、何でもあって。
cards.example_reading: とうきょう は ええ なあ、 なんでも あって。
cards.example_meaning: Tokyo's so lucky — it's got everything.
cards.pattern: ええ = いい

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): More Itomori-style endings: やけど for だけど, やで for だよ.
cards.context: Form: N / な-adj / plain + やけど (= だけど), + やで (= だよ). そうやけど = that's true, but…; 明日やで = it's tomorrow, you know. The same や that replaces だ.
cards.example_sentence: 今日は雨やけど、祭りは明日やで。
cards.example_reading: きょう は あめ やけど、 まつり は あした やで。
cards.example_meaning: It's raining today, but the festival's tomorrow, you know.
cards.pattern: N / plain + やけど (= だけど) · やで (= だよ)

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: 瀧 keeps thinking that, for a dream, everything feels far too real.
cards.context: Form: N / V plain form + にしては. The result doesn't match what you'd expect from that premise: 夢にしてはリアル, 初めてにしては上手. Compare 〜わりに (similar, but can follow adjectives: 高いわりに) and 〜としては (from the standpoint of).
cards.example_sentence: 初めて作ったにしては、このケーキはよくできている。
cards.example_reading: はじめて つくった に しては、 この ケーキ は よく できて いる。
cards.example_meaning: For a first attempt, this cake turned out really well.
cards.pattern: N / V plain form + にしては

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: The strange room, the strange body — 瀧 concludes it can only be a dream.
cards.context: Form: plain form (N / な-adj may drop だ) + としか思えない. Lit. 'can't think anything other than ~' — strong conviction, often about something odd. Same frame: 〜としか言えない 'all I can say is ~'.
cards.example_sentence: こんなに偶然が重なるなんて、運命としか思えない。
cards.example_reading: こんな に ぐうぜん が かさなる なんて、 うんめい と しか おもえない。
cards.example_meaning: With so many coincidences piling up, it can only be fate.
cards.pattern: plain form + としか思えない

meanings: to feel bewitched (as if tricked by a fox)
cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: The morning after a swap, each hero feels as if they had been tricked by a fox.
cards.context: Form: 狐につままれる, usually 狐につままれたような顔 / 気分. In folklore foxes 'pinch' (つまむ) people and bewitch them, so the idiom means being baffled by something that makes no sense. Fits a story steeped in the supernatural.
cards.example_sentence: 起きたら部屋がきれいに片付いていて、狐につままれたような気分だった。
cards.example_reading: おきたら へや が きれい に かたづいて いて、 きつね に つままれた よう な きぶん だった。
cards.example_meaning: I woke up to find my room neatly tidied, and felt completely bewildered.
cards.pattern: 狐につままれた(ような) + 顔／気分

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: 瀧 at 三葉's school — which desk was hers again? Which classroom?
cards.context: Form: plain form (often past: だった／したっけ) + っけ; polite 〜でしたっけ／〜ましたっけ. Asks yourself or someone to confirm something you half-remember. Very common in speech, never in formal writing.
cards.example_sentence: あれ、今日の集合時間は何時だったっけ？
cards.example_reading: あれ、 きょう の しゅうごう じかん は なんじ だった っけ？
cards.example_meaning: Huh, what time were we meeting today again?
cards.pattern: plain form (often past) + っけ

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: 四葉 has to call her big sister more than once, and she's running out of patience.
cards.context: Form: sentence + ってば (insisting: もういいってば！ 'I said it's fine!') or name + ってば (exasperation: お姉ちゃんってば…). Contracted from といえば. Softer variant: 〜ったら (お姉ちゃんったら).
cards.example_sentence: だから、私じゃないってば！
cards.example_reading: だから、 わたし じゃ ない って ば！
cards.example_meaning: I told you, it wasn't me!
cards.pattern: sentence / name + ってば

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Both heroes do things in each other's bodies that can't be undone — and talk about them in casual speech.
cards.context: Form: 〜てしまう → 〜ちゃう, 〜でしまう → 〜じゃう (past 〜ちゃった／〜じゃった). Completion or regret: 寝坊しちゃった, 全部飲んじゃった. A rougher male version is 〜ちまう／〜ちまった. Same meaning as 〜てしまう, but casual speech only.
cards.example_sentence: 楽しみにしていたプリン、弟に食べられちゃった。
cards.example_reading: たのしみ に して いた プリン、 おとうと に たべられちゃった。
cards.example_meaning: My little brother ate the pudding I'd been looking forward to.
cards.pattern: Vて → 〜ちゃう ／ Vで → 〜じゃう

meanings: neutral / feminine vs. boyish vs. rough masculine 'I'
cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: 三葉, in 瀧's body, tries several words for 'I' before landing on 俺 — while 瀧 says 俺 with 三葉's voice.
cards.context: Form: chosen by speaker, setting and self-image. わたし = neutral; standard for women, and for men in formal settings. わたくし = very formal. あたし = casual feminine. 僕 = soft, polite boyish. 俺 = rough, masculine, among friends. A boy saying わたし casually to his friends sounds odd, so the wrong pronoun instantly marks someone as 'not themselves'.
cards.example_sentence: 仕事では「わたし」と言うが、友達とは「俺」で話している。
cards.example_reading: しごと で は 「わたし」 と いう が、 ともだち と は 「おれ」 で はなして いる。
cards.example_meaning: At work I use the neutral word for 'I', but with friends I use the rough, masculine one.
cards.pattern: わたし／わたくし／あたし／僕／俺

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Rough male endings like these are part of what makes 'Mitsuha' sound so unlike herself at school.
cards.context: Form: plain form + ぞ／ぜ (after nouns and な-adj: だぞ, だぜ). ぞ = forceful assertion or warning (行くぞ！ 'Let's go!', 危ないぞ 'Watch out'). ぜ = cool, matey emphasis (行こうぜ). Both sound masculine; a softer, neutral choice is よ.
cards.example_sentence: もう遅いぞ。早く帰ろうぜ。
cards.example_reading: もう おそい ぞ。 はやく かえろう ぜ。
cards.example_meaning: It's late, you know. Let's head home already.
cards.pattern: plain form + ぞ／ぜ

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: The breezy speech of 瀧's Tokyo friends, which 三葉 has to keep up with.
cards.context: Form: plain form (N / な-adj without だ) + じゃん. From じゃないか; originally Kanto-area slang. Points out the obvious or seeks agreement: いいじゃん！ 'That's great!', 言ったじゃん 'I told you!'. Used by both genders, but very casual.
cards.example_sentence: その服、すごく似合ってるじゃん。
cards.example_reading: その ふく、 すごく にあってる じゃん。
cards.example_meaning: Those clothes really suit you!
cards.pattern: plain form (N / な-adj without だ) + じゃん

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Rough reactions of disbelief — the voice of a boy waking up in a world that makes no sense.
cards.context: Form: plain form (N / な-adj without だ) + かよ. Rhetorical か + emphatic よ: surprise, disbelief or irritation. マジかよ 'No way!', また〜かよ 'Not ~ again!'. Masculine and rough; the neutral version is just a rising tone (本当？).
cards.example_sentence: また雨かよ。せっかくの休みなのに。
cards.example_reading: また あめ かよ。 せっかく の やすみ な のに。
cards.example_meaning: Rain again? And on my day off, too.
cards.pattern: plain form + かよ

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: 'Taki' suddenly seems oddly girlish to his friends, and 'Mitsuha' boyish to hers.
cards.context: Form: N + っぽい (男っぽい 'boyish', 子供っぽい 'childish'); Vます-stem + っぽい (忘れっぽい 'forgetful'); plain sentence + っぽい (casual 'seems like': 雨が降るっぽい). Vague and casual — compare 〜らしい, which means 'typical of, as it should be' (男らしい 'manly', usually praise).
cards.example_sentence: 今日の彼、なんだか女の子っぽいね。
cards.example_reading: きょう の かれ、 なんだか おんなのこ っぽい ね。
cards.example_meaning: He seems kind of girlish today, doesn't he?
cards.pattern: N / Vます-stem / plain form + っぽい

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: As 'Taki' works the needle, the tear in 奥寺先輩's skirt becomes something pretty before everyone's eyes.
cards.context: Form: 見る見る(うちに) + a verb of change (〜なる, 〜ていく). Describes a fast change you can actually watch happen: 見る見るうちに暗くなった. Often written みるみる. Compare あっという間に (in an instant, not necessarily watched).
cards.example_sentence: 薬を飲んだら、熱が見る見るうちに下がった。
cards.example_reading: くすり を のんだら、 ねつ が みるみる うち に さがった。
cards.example_meaning: After I took the medicine, my fever went down rapidly.
cards.pattern: 見る見る(うちに) + change verb

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Back in their own bodies, each grumbles about what the other did with their day.
cards.context: Form: plain form (N / な-adj + な) + のに at the end of a sentence. The main clause is swallowed, leaving regret, complaint or disappointment: 言ってくれればよかったのに 'You should have told me', せっかく作ったのに 'And after I made it specially…'. Different from mid-sentence のに 'even though'.
cards.example_sentence: 早く起きれば間に合ったのに。
cards.example_reading: はやく おきれば まにあった のに。
cards.example_meaning: If only I'd got up earlier, I would have made it.
cards.pattern: plain form + のに。(at sentence end)

meanings: to have no recollection of doing it
cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Friends describe things 'they' did yesterday that neither hero remembers doing.
cards.context: Form: 身に覚えがない, or before a noun 身に覚えのない + N. Lit. 'no memory in one's own body' — something is pinned on you that you didn't do (or can't remember doing). Common in denials: 身に覚えのない罪 'a crime I didn't commit'.
cards.example_sentence: 身に覚えのない請求書が届いて、驚いた。
cards.example_reading: み に おぼえ の ない せいきゅうしょ が とどいて、 おどろいた。
cards.example_meaning: I was shocked when a bill arrived for something I never bought.
cards.pattern: 身に覚えがない ／ 身に覚えのない + N

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Swapping bodies with a stranger in your sleep? That can't possibly be real — can it?
cards.context: Form: plain form (N + の／である, な-adj + な) + わけがない (casual: わけない). A flat denial based on reasoning. 〜はずがない is close but leans on expectation; 〜わけではない means 'it's not that ~' — don't mix them up.
cards.example_sentence: こんなに難しい問題、一日で解けるわけがない。
cards.example_reading: こんな に むずかしい もんだい、 いちにち で とける わけ が ない。
cards.example_meaning: There's no way I can solve a problem this hard in one day.
cards.pattern: plain form + わけがない

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Friends' strange reports, odd notes, lost days — slowly the pieces begin to add up.
cards.context: Form: 辻褄が合う／合わない, 辻褄を合わせる (to make a story fit). 辻 (crossroads) + 褄 (the hem of a kimono): seams that line up. Usually about stories or explanations. Often written in kana: つじつま.
cards.example_sentence: 彼の説明は、どうも辻褄が合わない。
cards.example_reading: かれ の せつめい は、 どうも つじつま が あわない。
cards.example_meaning: His explanation just doesn't add up.
cards.pattern: 辻褄が合う ／ 合わない ／ 辻褄を合わせる

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: The chapter's turning point — could it be that they really are swapping?
cards.context: Form: まさか + negative guess (まさか来ないだろう 'surely he won't come'), まさか〜とは思わなかった 'I never dreamed ~', or alone as an exclamation 'No way!'. Trailing off — まさか… — signals someone realising something unbelievable.
cards.example_sentence: まさか、あれが本当に夢じゃなかったなんて。
cards.example_reading: まさか、 あれ が ほんとう に ゆめ じゃ なかった なんて。
cards.example_meaning: No way — that really wasn't a dream?
cards.pattern: まさか + 〜ない／〜とは思わなかった／…

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: At first each tries to brush off the strange signs as nothing more than imagination.
cards.context: Form: 気のせいだ 'it's just my imagination'; 気のせいか、〜 'maybe it's just me, but ~'. A way to dismiss a strange feeling — exactly what you tell yourself before admitting something impossible.
cards.example_sentence: 気のせいか、今日はみんなが私を見ている気がする。
cards.example_reading: き の せい か、 きょう は みんな が わたし を みて いる き が する。
cards.example_meaning: Maybe it's just me, but I feel like everyone's looking at me today.
cards.pattern: 気のせいだ ／ 気のせいか、〜
